replace: // mutant: a second job may start while one is active
note: The settings queue has one active job. Without the early return in drain(), every admit starts its own job, so back-to-back writes read the same stored value and overlap their physical writes (T-07-14, COMPAT-03). Measured by the peak count of concurrent physical writes.

expected_failure.test: three back-to-back writes are applied in arrival order with no overlapping physical write

replace: // mutant: the next job does not wait for the issued write
note: A deadline answers the requester unknown but does not cancel an issued write. Without awaiting the physical write before releasing the writer, the next job reads storage before the earlier write lands and can decide on a value that is about to be replaced (T-07-14). Measured by the second job reading before the first write is released.

expected_failure.test: the next job waits for the previous physical write even after that requester was answered unknown

note: The compare-and-swap check runs inside the drained job, against the revision just read. Always accepting the revision lets a writer holding a stale revision overwrite a newer edit from another window (D-16, T-07-14). Measured with a test-only cas key: a stale revision must answer conflict and write nothing.

expected_failure.test: a cas key saves with revision + 1 only when the request holds the stored revision (D-16)

note: Choosing the value already in effect writes nothing (D-11, COMPAT-02): on a fresh install re-selecting the default stores nothing. Without the equality skip every choice is written, so a fresh install gains a stored key the agent never changed (T-07-15). Measured with a test-only key over absent storage.

expected_failure.test: the value already in effect writes nothing, and switching back to the default writes it explicitly (D-11)

note: The one settings write primitive names the local area. Swapping it for sync would copy settings to Google servers, against DATA-01 and D-03 (T-07-16). The tracer world records any sync, session or managed access as a forbidden channel, and the worker-level sequence asserts none was reached.

expected_failure.test: after a sequence of settings operations only storage.local was written, one key per write (DATA-01)

note: An extension page open in a tab is a top-frame tab document with the extension's own id, so v1's fromContent admits it as content. Without the isAgentDocument(sender.url) clause, a status hint from any document in a tab, whatever its URL, projects that tab (T-07-12, D-17). Measured by the action log growing for a sender identical to the content script except for its URL.

expected_failure.test: a status hint from a sender identical to the content script except for its URL is refused (D-17)

note: The manifest injects only into https agent documents, so a content message from a plain-http document on the same host and path did not come from the content script. Weakening the protocol comparison to any http scheme admits it (T-07-12, D-17). Measured by the plain-http case, the only refused sender that differs from the genuine one by its protocol alone.

expected_failure.test: a status hint from a sender identical to the content script except for its URL is refused (D-17)

note: fromOptions deliberately does not require sender.tab to be undefined, because an options page opened in a tab carries one. Its exact packaged URL is therefore the only thing that separates it from a content script or any other document running as this extension. Without the URL clause, every sender with the extension's own id may write settings (T-07-13, D-17). Measured by a set-setting from the genuine content sender being answered and written.

expected_failure.test: set-setting is admitted only from the packaged popup or the packaged options page (D-17, D-18)

note: The settings read gates the first tint, and a read whose callback never arrives must not hold rows untinted for longer than SETTINGS_READ_TIMEOUT_MS (D-09, COMPAT-04). Without the time-bound callback opening the gate, a hung settings read leaves the page untinted for the life of the document. Measured with a hung read under fake timers: the rows must be tinted once the bound has passed.

expected_failure.test: a hung settings read holds rows untinted for at most the time bound, then tints and leaves no timer

note: The controller runs only once the settings read has settled, so the first tint is painted with the settings in effect rather than repainted when they land (D-09, COMPAT-04). Without settingsReady in runnable(), a confirmed preference tints before the settings read has answered. Measured with the settings read held while the preference is already confirmed: no row may carry a marker yet.

expected_failure.test: the first tint waits for the settings read even when the preference is already confirmed

note: A failed settings read is treated as every key at its default, and it opens the gate at once: an agent whose storage cannot be read sees 0.1.0 tinting with no wait (D-08, D-09, COMPAT-04). If a read that reports chrome.runtime.lastError no longer lands, the page waits out the whole time bound before it tints. Measured with a rejected read well inside the bound: every row must already be tinted.

expected_failure.test: a rejected settings read tints with no wait

note: An absent key means its default, applied on read, with no install-time write (D-04, COMPAT-02). The status is what later phases use to tell a fresh or 0.1.0 install apart from a damaged value (D-12), so an absent theme must resolve as default, never as unreadable. Measured on the shipped theme key with nothing stored.

expected_failure.test: an absent theme resolves to Classic by default, and the stored Classic form resolves as stored

note: A value written by a newer Zhroma is unreadable here and is never migrated down (D-08): its fields may mean something this version does not know, so the agent sees the default, and the stored bytes stay for the newer version to read again. Without the upper bound on v, a newer theme form that happens to parse is accepted as stored. Measured on the shipped theme key with the newer-v row of the rejection table.

expected_failure.test: a newer v resolves to the Classic default as unreadable, without touching the stored value
